text: ABA Model Rule 1.1 - Competence. A lawyer shall provide competent representation to a client, requiring legal knowledge, skill, thoroughness, and preparation reasonably necessary for the representation.

ABA Model Rule 1.4 - Communication. A lawyer shall promptly inform the client of any decision or circumstance requiring informed consent, reasonably consult about means of representation, and keep client informed of case status.

ABA Model Rule 1.5 - Fees. A lawyer shall not make an agreement for, charge, or collect an unreasonable fee. Factors include time, novelty, skill required, fee customarily charged, and results obtained.

ABA Model Rule 1.6 - Confidentiality of Information. A lawyer shall not reveal information relating to representation of a client unless the client gives informed consent, the disclosure is impliedly authorized, or an exception applies.

ABA Model Rule 1.7 - Conflict of Interest: Current Clients. A lawyer shall not represent a client if representation involves a concurrent conflict of interest unless conditions for informed consent are met.

ABA Model Rule 1.8 - Conflict of Interest: Current Clients: Specific Rules. Prohibits business transactions with clients, using client information to client's disadvantage, soliciting gifts, and other specific conflict scenarios.

ABA Model Rule 1.9 - Duties to Former Clients. A lawyer shall not represent a person in the same or substantially related matter where the former client's interests are materially adverse, without former client consent.

ABA Model Rule 1.10 - Imputation of Conflicts. While lawyers are associated in a firm, none shall knowingly represent a client when any one of them practicing alone would be prohibited from doing so by Rules 1.7 or 1.9.

ABA Model Rule 1.15 - Safekeeping Property. A lawyer shall hold property of clients separate from lawyer's own property. Funds shall be kept in separate trust account (IOLTA). Complete records maintained for 5 years.

ABA Model Rule 3.1 - Meritorious Claims and Contentions. A lawyer shall not bring or defend a proceeding, or assert or controvert an issue therein, unless there is a basis in law and fact for doing so that is not frivolous.
ABA Model Rule 3.3 - Candor Toward the Tribunal. A lawyer shall not knowingly make a false statement of fact or law to a tribunal, fail to correct a false statement, or offer false evidence.

ABA Model Rule 3.4 - Fairness to Opposing Party and Counsel. A lawyer shall not unlawfully obstruct access to evidence, falsify evidence, counsel witnesses to testify falsely, or violate discovery rules.

ABA Model Rule 4.1 - Truthfulness in Statements to Others. A lawyer shall not knowingly make a false statement of material fact or law to a third person, or fail to disclose material facts to avoid client fraud.

ABA Model Rule 5.1 - Responsibilities of Partners and Supervisory Lawyers. Partners shall ensure firm has measures to assure all lawyers conform to professional conduct rules. Direct supervisory responsibility.

ABA Model Rule 5.3 - Responsibilities Regarding Nonlawyer Assistance. Lawyer with supervisory authority over nonlawyer shall ensure person's conduct is compatible with professional obligations of the lawyer.

FRCP Rule 11 - Signing Pleadings. Attorney certifies to best of knowledge that filing is not for improper purpose, claims warranted by law, factual contentions have evidentiary support. Sanctions for violations.

FRCP Rule 26(a) - Initial Disclosures. Parties must disclose names of individuals with discoverable information, copies of documents, computation of damages, and insurance agreements within 14 days of Rule 26(f) conference.

FRCP Rule 26(b)(5) - Privilege Claims. Party withholding information on privilege grounds must expressly make the claim and describe the nature of withheld documents in a manner enabling assessment of the claim.

FRCP Rule 37 - Discovery Sanctions. Court may compel discovery and impose sanctions including attorney fees, adverse inference instructions, striking pleadings, default judgment, or contempt for failure to comply.

28 U.S.C. 1927 - Vexatious Litigation. Any attorney who so multiplies proceedings unreasonably and vexatiously may be required to satisfy personally the excess costs, expenses, and attorney fees attributable to such conduct.
Firm Policy FP-CONF-01: All client communications must be marked ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL. External communications reviewed by supervising attorney before transmission.
Firm Policy FP-CONF-02: Privileged attorney work product must never be included in billing descriptions, court filings, or client-facing status memos without partner review and approval.

Firm Policy FP-TRUST-01: All trust account transactions require three-way reconciliation (bank statement, client ledger, firm ledger). Monthly reconciliation mandatory. Discrepancies reported within 24 hours.
Firm Policy FP-TRUST-02: No disbursement from trust account without written client authorization and supervising attorney approval. Settlement disbursements require partner sign-off.
Firm Policy FP-CONFLICT-01: Conflict checks mandatory before accepting any new matter. Check must include all parties, affiliates, and related entities. Results documented in matter file.
Firm Policy FP-CONFLICT-02: Ethical wall procedures required when lateral hire brings potential conflicts. Information barriers documented and circulated. Periodic compliance audits.
Firm Policy FP-FILING-01: All court filings require supervising attorney review and approval before submission. Emergency filings require verbal approval documented within 24 hours.
Firm Policy FP-FILING-02: Electronic court filings must comply with local court CM/ECF requirements. Filing confirmation saved to matter file within 1 business day.
Firm Policy FP-BILLING-01: Time entries must be recorded daily. Descriptions must be sufficiently detailed for client review but must not contain privileged strategy information.
Firm Policy FP-BILLING-02: Invoices reviewed by billing partner before submission. Block billing prohibited. Minimum billing increment: 0.1 hours (6 minutes).
Firm Policy FP-DEADLINE-01: All litigation deadlines entered in centralized calendar system within 24 hours of discovery. Backup attorney assigned for all critical deadlines.
Firm Policy FP-DEADLINE-02: Statute of limitations tracked from matter inception. Two-week advance warning for all SOL deadlines. Partner notification at 30, 14, and 7 days.
Firm Policy FP-RECORD-01: Matter files maintained per retention schedule. Litigation files: 7 years post-closure. Transactional files: 10 years. Tax files: permanent.
Firm Policy FP-RECORD-02: Client documents returned upon matter closure. Firm work product retained per retention schedule. Privileged materials archived in restricted access storage.
Firm Policy FP-CLOSE-01: Matter closure checklist required for all matters. Final billing submitted within 30 days. Trust account reconciled and closed. Client closing letter sent.
Firm Policy FP-DATA-01: Client data classified as confidential. Multi-factor authentication required for remote access. Data at rest encrypted with AES-256. Annual security audit.
Firm Policy FP-DATA-02: No client data stored on personal devices. Cloud storage only in firm-approved platforms (Firm DMS, NetDocuments). USB export requires IT approval.

IOLTA Compliance: Interest on Lawyers Trust Accounts must comply with state bar IOLTA program requirements. Nominal or short-term funds deposited in IOLTA account. Client notification of IOLTA participation.
Anti-Money Laundering: Firm must exercise due diligence to ensure client funds are not proceeds of criminal activity. Enhanced due diligence for international transactions exceeding $10,000.
Sarbanes-Oxley Section 307: Attorney appearing before SEC on behalf of issuer must report evidence of material violation up the ladder to CLO and, if necessary, to audit committee or board.
FCPA Compliance: Firm personnel must not directly or indirectly make payments to foreign officials. Due diligence required for foreign agents and consultants. Annual FCPA training mandatory.
GDPR Compliance: Client data of EU persons processed in accordance with GDPR requirements. Data processing agreements with vendors. Right to erasure honored upon request.
State Bar CLE Requirements: All attorneys must complete minimum continuing legal education hours per bar jurisdiction. Ethics component mandatory. Tracking and reporting by firm CLE coordinator.
Professional Liability Insurance: Firm maintains minimum $10M per occurrence, $25M aggregate professional liability coverage. All matters within coverage scope. Claims reported within 48 hours.

Firm Policy FP-AI-01: AI-generated legal research must be independently verified against primary sources before inclusion in any filing, memo, or client communication. AI hallucination check mandatory.
Firm Policy FP-AI-02: No confidential client information submitted to external AI platforms without client consent and data processing agreement. Firm-approved AI tools only.
Litigation Hold Protocol: Preservation notice issued within 24 hours of reasonably anticipated litigation. IT department notified to suspend auto-deletion. Custodian acknowledgments tracked.

Firm Policy FP-SIGN-01: Document execution requires verification of signatory authority. Wet-ink signatures for real property transactions in jurisdictions requiring notarization. E-signatures per E-SIGN Act.
Firm Policy FP-SCOPE-01: Matter scope defined in engagement letter. Scope changes require written amendment. Out-of-scope work requires client consent before commencement.
Firm Policy FP-DIVERSITY-01: Pro bono commitment of minimum 50 hours per attorney annually. Diversity initiatives tracked. Equity in matter assignment and professional development opportunities.
